what: CGI is a Canadian information technology and business consulting company. It builds and runs software systems for governments, banks, insurers and utilities, with a model of owning client relationships locally.
customers: Governments, financial institutions, utilities, manufacturers and health organisations, mostly in Canada, the United States and Europe.
money: Managed IT and business process services
running clients' systems and processes under long contracts
moat: Long-term outsourcing contracts with governments and regulated industries, where security clearances and institutional knowledge make switching slow and risky.
risks: Government budget cycles determine contract timing
Revenue grew only about 4% last year
Artificial intelligence may reduce the people-hours a contract requires
Only three analysts cover it in this data
opportunities: Net margin of 11% is strong for an IT services company
A long record of acquiring regional IT firms and raising their margins
Cash of about $1.1 billion against $2 billion of debt is manageable
watch: Bookings as a share of revenue and organic growth in constant currency.
